question:
A 79-year-old woman presents for follow-up regarding her hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She was
started on chlorthalidone six months ago due to consistently elevated blood pressure and atorvastatin
20 mg daily after a fasting lipid panel revealed a total cholesterol level of 260 mg/dL (reference range:
125–200), LDL cholesterol of 179 mg/dL (< 130), and HDL cholesterol of 42 mg/dL (≥ 46). A
comprehensive metabolic panel, including liver enzymes and fasting blood glucose, was normal prior to
starting these medications. The patient has a family history of coronary artery disease, does not
consume alcohol, and quit smoking several years ago. She reports feeling well and is not taking any
other medications. Her current laboratory results are as follows: | | Patient value | Reference range | |
--- | --- | --- | | Aspartate aminotransferase (U/liter) | 74 | 0–35 | | Alanine aminotransferase (U/liter) | 83 |
0–35 | | Alkaline phosphatase (U/liter) | 88 | 30–120 | | Total bilirubin (mg/dL) | 0.9 | 0.3–1.0 | | LDL
cholesterol (mg/dL) | 110 | < 130 | What is the most appropriate management approach for this patient?
Answer Choices: (A) Discontinue atorvastatin immediately (B) Replace atorvastatin with pravastatin (C)
Order creatine kinase levels (D) Continue with current medications (E) Increase atorvastatin dose (F)
Switch to a non-statin lipid-lowering agent (G) Add CoQ10 supplementation (H) Halve the dose of
atorvastatin (I) Switch to rosuvastatin (J) Add ezetimibe
 A. Add ezetimibe
